notes: Added for relation-property coverage (ids 0013-0016): an ABox inheritance edit. The edit moves an individual battle from one class (battles of the American Revolutionary War) to another (battles of the War of 1812), and both determinate queries ask what that class gives its members: its time span (fol + temporal, a date comparison) and the presidency it falls in (dl: the class lies within Madison's presidency). The War of 1812 keeps the same opponents (Americans against the British), so the edit breaks the battle's date and its place in the siege of Boston but not its belligerents; those two go with the edit as side facts of the battle. Derivability unlikely: stated everywhere, but recoverable from the battle's date. Worlds: Warren's death is stored through the battle (w1) or with its own date and war (w2), in which case 'Warren fell at Bunker Hill' gives way. Both are consistent with firm facts outside the chain: Warren's other acts (the Suffolk Resolves, sending Paul Revere) all fall in 1774-75 and do not need him to die then. R1: the War of 1812 ran from June 1812 to February 1815 (Treaty of Ghent ratified), with a few naval actions into mid-1815; every battle falls in the nineteenth century and inside Madison's presidency (March 1809 to March 1817). Lexington and Concord (near query) were fought in April 1775, before Bunker Hill; their war differs from the new answer. Breed's Hill is not asked about.
